_status: NEW 2026-08-05. Depth pass on the United Kingdom — the corpus's first non-EU-member municipal/regional government-finance chain, following the Netherlands pass the same day. UK chosen (of Switzerland, Norway, UK scouted) for zero language barrier and for being the corpus's only *former* EU member.
_note: Three general-purpose subagents researched this in parallel (Fair Funding Review 2.0 Technical Annexes / RO returns; CIPFA Code and council accounts / VOA valuation chain; RO-returns methodology / UKSPF-EU-structural-funds succession), briefed with this project's extraction rules. EVERY quote below marked 'VERIFIED DIRECTLY' was independently re-confirmed by this session against the primary source's own raw text (legislation.gov.uk and gov.uk HTML stripped of tags, or PDFs downloaded and text-extracted with pypdf) — the same discipline applied to the Netherlands pass the same day, after that session found AI-summarized WebFetch quotes are not reliably verbatim. Two council-accounts quotes (Wolverhampton) and all legislation.gov.uk / gov.uk statistics-page quotes were re-verified; one alternate council (York) reported by a subagent was NOT independently re-verified and is not used as edge evidence, only noted.

reports.title: Technical Annex on the Adult Social Care Relative Needs Formula (ASC RNF)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG)
reports.description: Technical annex to the Fair Funding Review 2.0 consultation, feeding the Local Government Finance Settlement's Adult Social Care funding formula. Its §5 'Data and technical definitions' is a per-indicator data-source table naming exact statistical releases and table codes — this branch's UK analog to the Dutch Toelichting and Ontario's OMPF Appendix F. VERIFIED DIRECTLY: PDF downloaded and text-extracted in full (pypdf).
reports.cadence_note: Published as part of the Fair Funding Review 2.0 consultation cycle rather than a fixed annual schedule; filed as annual as the nearest available cadence.

reports.title: Local authority revenue expenditure and financing, England
reports.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG)
reports.description: MHCLG's compiled national statistical release of English local-authority revenue expenditure and financing — the direct structural parallel to Alberta's `ab-municipalaffairs-financial-statistical-data` and the Netherlands' `nl-cbs-iv3-gemeenten`. Accredited Official Statistics under the Statistics and Registration Service Act 2007. VERIFIED DIRECTLY: technical-notes page fetched and parsed in full.
reports.cadence_note: Published in stages through the year — a first release (early-September data cut-off) and a second/final release (mid-November cut-off) per financial year, per the technical notes' own 'Response rate and grossing' section.

reports.title: Revenue Outturn (RO) forms
reports.description: The standardised financial return every English local authority must complete annually, covering general fund revenue account transactions — the direct English counterpart to Alberta's Financial Information Return (FIR) and the Netherlands' Iv3-rapportage.
reports.cadence_note: Submitted in two stages per financial year: provisional figures (deadline late July) then certified figures (deadline mid-October), per MHCLG's technical notes.

reports.title: Estimates of the population for England and Wales
reports.description: ONS's annual mid-year population estimates by single year of age, cited by exact title in the ASC RNF technical annex as the source for its population-based need indicators. VERIFIED DIRECTLY in the ASC RNF PDF's own §5 data-source table.

reports.title: Census 2021
reports.description: The decennial UK census. Cited repeatedly by exact Nomis table code in the ASC RNF technical annex's §5 data-source table (e.g. RM066 'Living arrangements by age', RM121 'Sex by age', RM201 'Tenure by age'), and used to rebase ONS's own population projections for the RNF's age-based indicators. VERIFIED DIRECTLY.

reports.title: Adult Social Care Activity and Finance Report
reports.description: NHS England Digital's annual report on adult social care activity and finance, cited by exact table number (Table 38: 'Number of clients accessing long term support at the end of the year, by age band and support setting') in the ASC RNF technical annex. VERIFIED DIRECTLY.

reports.title: Code of Practice on Local Authority Accounting in the United Kingdom (the Code)
reports.description: The accounting standard every English local authority's Statement of Accounts must follow — the UK functional equivalent of `psab-psas` and the Netherlands' `nl-bbv`. Legal basis, VERIFIED DIRECTLY (legislation.gov.uk): Local Government Act 2003 s.21(2) creates the 'proper practices' concept and delegates identifying the actual standard to regulations; The Local Authorities (Capital Finance and Accounting) (England) Regulations 2003, reg. 31 names the CIPFA Code specifically as that standard. Note: this is a two-instrument statutory chain, not one — the Accounts and Audit Regulations 2015 uses the phrase 'proper practices' but does not itself name CIPFA in the provisions checked this session.
reports.cadence_note: Issued in dated annual editions (e.g. '2024/25', '2026/27'), unlike the Netherlands' BBV which amends continuously without dated editions.

reports.title: Statement of Accounts 2024-25 (City of Wolverhampton Council)
reports.description: Chosen as the exemplar English local authority, the way Nijmegen is the exemplar Dutch municipality and Grande Prairie the exemplar Alberta one — its own accounting-policy notes and auditor's opinion both name the CIPFA/LASAAC Code by dated edition. VERIFIED DIRECTLY: 311-page PDF downloaded and text-extracted in full (pypdf); the Code is named 15+ times through the document.

reports.title: Local Non-Domestic Rating List / Council Tax Valuation List
reports.description: The national property-valuation function underlying both Council Tax bands and Business Rates rateable values — the UK functional equivalent of the Netherlands' `nl-wet-woz` and Ontario's `mpac-assessment`. Legal basis, VERIFIED DIRECTLY (legislation.gov.uk): Local Government Finance Act 1992 ss.20-23 (Council Tax valuation lists) and Local Government Finance Act 1988 ss.41, 61 and Sch.6 (business-rates rating lists and the 'rateable value' definition). NOTE ON NAMING: neither Act uses the literal string 'Valuation Office Agency' in the sections checked — both instead say 'the Commissioners of Inland Revenue' / 'the valuation officer' / 'listing officer'. 'Valuation Office Agency' as a literal name only appears in downstream documents (see `uk-stevenage-nndr1`) — flagged per this project's own tense/naming-precision convention rather than silently modernised.
reports.cadence_note: Business-rates rating lists are compiled on a multi-year revaluation cycle (1988 Act s.41(2): 1 April 1990 and every fifth year after, subject to later amendment); Council Tax valuation lists are maintained continuously. Filed as annual as the nearest practical cadence.

reports.title: Non-Domestic Rates (NDR) 2026/27 / Tax Base (Stevenage Borough Council)
reports.description: A council officer decision report on the annual NNDR1 business-rates return, chosen as the exemplar document naming the VOA directly (Wolverhampton's own accounts do not name VOA/rateable values in the sections checked this session — the two councils supply different halves of the UK chain). VERIFIED DIRECTLY: 22-page PDF downloaded and text-extracted (pypdf).

_dropped.edge: UK Shared Prosperity Fund (UKSPF) succeeds EU structural funds (ERDF/ESF)
_dropped.why: UPDATED 2026-08-06. The original objection — 'does not fit this corpus's relationship_type ontology (calculated_from | uses_data_from | methodology_depends_on | cites — none of which mean replaces or succeeds)' — has been resolved at the schema level: `supersedes` is now a `RelationType` and this corpus has a parallel unweighted `relations` list to hold it. See `notes/SCHEMA-DECISION-relationship-types.md` and `src/lib/types.ts`. THIS CASE STILL CANNOT BE MINTED, for a reason the original note did not identify: NEITHER END IS A NODE. There is no `gb-ukspf-prospectus` and no node for the EU structural funds, so a relation would dangle at both ends and the loader would drop it. It is therefore reclassified from `note` to `no-node-yet` — a research lead with a known shape, not an ontology problem. The evidence is unchanged and the conflict in it is unchanged: the UKSPF prospectus's ministerial foreword states "This is our vision and ambition for the new £2.6 billion UK Shared Prosperity Fund (UKSPF), which succeeds the old EU structural funds" (VERIFIED DIRECTLY, gov.uk fetched and parsed), while the UKSPF's own FAQ page states, also VERIFIED DIRECTLY, "The UKSPF is not a direct replacement for EU structural funds." Two primary UK-government documents holding different framings of the same relationship, reported per `Research.1.md` §3 and not adjudicated — and note that this conflict is now a second-order problem: it decides what the relation's `basis` should say, not whether the relation can exist. Neither document names ERDF or ESF anywhere in the text fetched; a targeted search for those acronyms in both returned NOT FOUND. A subagent (not independently re-verified) reported an Orkney Islands Council committee report naming both "European Regional Development Fund (ERDF)" and "European Social Fund (ESF)" as the programmes UKSPF and the Levelling Up Fund replace. WHAT UNBLOCKS THIS: two nodes. The UKSPF prospectus is recurrently published and is the easy one.

_dropped.edge: uk-mhclg-asc-rnf-annex's sibling CYPS (Children and Young People's Services) Relative Needs Formula annex -> National Pupil Database / Children in Need (CiN) / Children Looked After (CLA)
_dropped.why: The CYPS RNF technical note (https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/the-fair-funding-review-20/f-technical-annex-on-the-children-and-young-peoples-services-cyps-relative-needs-formula-rnf) names "the National Pupil Database", "Children in Need (CiN)" and "Children Looked After (CLA)" datasets by title/acronym, and Census 2021 again, but — unlike the ASC RNF annex's §5 — does not give exact table/release codes in the passage found. Real leads, not yet independently re-verified by this session (subagent extraction only), and no nodes exist yet for the three named datasets. Worth a second annex-by-annex pass — the Fair Funding Review 2.0 consultation apparently has one technical annex per service area (Adult Social Care done this session; Children's Services, Highways Maintenance and others not yet opened).

_dropped.edge: uk-la-ro-form -> uk-cipfa-code (CIPFA as RO-return co-validator, not methodology source)
_dropped.why: The RO technical notes state (VERIFIED DIRECTLY) that submitted RO figures are "subjected to rigorous pre-defined validation tests... by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG) and the Chartered Institute of Public Finance and Accounting (CIPFA) as the data are received and processed." This is CIPFA acting as a data-quality co-reviewer of the RO returns, not a methodology CIPFA's Code prescribes for the returns themselves the way it does for a Statement of Accounts — a different relationship than `uk-wolverhampton-statement-of-accounts -> uk-cipfa-code`, and not minted as its own edge to avoid conflating the two.
